summary: Two series Josephson junctions with areas scaled in ratio $\alpha$ can be reduced to a single effective high-transparency element with $\mathcal{T} = 4\alpha/(1+\alpha)^2$, whose validity under dynamical drive is systematically investigated through normalized voltage-waveform RMS error. The reduction remains accurate to $\epsilon_V \lesssim 10^{-4}$–$10^{-5}$ over broad frequency and amplitude ranges but breaks down in the strongly nonlinear near-resonant regime where internal relative-phase dynamics emerge.
motivation: Engineering nonsinusoidal current-phase relations from conventional junctions is useful for tailoring superconducting nonlinearities, but the validity of the static CPR mapping to finite-frequency drive with finite capacitance and dissipation must be established before deploying synthetic elements as circuit blocks.
method: Full two-junction RCSJ equations with $I_{c1} = 2\ \mu$A, $C_1 = 200$ fF, $R_1 = R_2 = 20$ k$\Omega$ are compared numerically to an effective single-junction model derived by requiring equal electrostatic energy and dissipated power; comparison is quantified via normalized RMS error between complete and effective voltage waveforms over $\alpha \in \{0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.99\}$, drive frequencies $0.05 \lesssim \Omega \lesssim 1.05$, and amplitudes $10^{-3} \lesssim i_{ac} \lesssim 0.5$.
result: High-accuracy region extends to low normalized drive frequency with $\epsilon_V$ near numerical floor; accuracy deteriorates approaching the plasma resonance $\Omega_p = 1$ and at large drive amplitudes, with superharmonic structures near $\Omega \approx 1/3$; agreement improves markedly as $\alpha \to 1$, approaching exact equivalence in the symmetric limit.
